IMO and in no particular order:

  • Bodyweight Exercise - Start out slow and work up to Dragon Flags, Human Flags and Handstand Pushups. You'd be amazed at what the human body can achieve if you set reasonable goals and work hard for thirty minutes every day. Use this infographic (not mine) for good workout guidlines. Best thing about bodyweight is that stairs, bars, walls, trees, benches, signposts, anything in your local area becomes workout equipment, it's just up to you to create a way to use it!

  • Programming - If you have the mind, the knack and the drive for it, programming can be one of the most creative and enjoyable activities. It's a little bit of problem solving, a little bit of typing and a whole lot of logic. I first got into it with Python and then moved onto these C++ Tutorials. I highly recommend giving it a shot as with even a little bit of programming experience under your belt you can solve problems you never even knew existed. Best thing about programming? You have a computer, you can program, download an IDE, open up the documentation, open up some youtube tutorials and when you're good enough you can do it anywhere.

  • Reading - Infinite Jest is available free online in pdf form so why are you even still here? Go. Now. If not for me then think of the poor Voat servers.

  • Writing - There's a reason it was invented almost four thousand years ago and is still the number one method of relaying information in the civilised world. You are reading my writing right now, and I'm only writing because I read someone else's (Here's looking at you OP). Writing isn't just about expressing the self, it's about exploring the human condition in ways you simply cant through speech alone. Writing may not be 'fun' for everyone, but for those who enjoy it, it can be relaxing, exciting, thrilling and profound. And once again, all you need is paper or a laptop. Get to work.

  • Meditation - Again not for everyone but I highly recommend practising mindfulness for at least twenty minutes a day. It's not fun as much as it is awe-inspiring. It can be difficult at first but using resources like this can help get you in the mood.

  • Urban Exploration - This ones self explanatory. Get yourself a decent jacket, jeans, boots, gloves and a backpack. If you can get in just by walking and without seeing any obvious 'Do Not Tresspass' signs you can pretty easily pass yourself off as lost. If you're exploring anywhere abandoned, bring at least one friend, alcohol for cleaning wounds, bandages, plenty of water, a torch, a cell phone with a backup battery, energy bars and a multimeter (for checking live wires) if you can afford one. The more you enjoy it, the more you can afford to drop on it. It can be truly breathtaking or terrifying depending on where you explore.

  • Neature Walk - This explains everything

  • Watching Reddit Burn - This one's self explanatory. But watch it from here, don't give them the traffic.

  • Travelling - Go to the airport and ask if there are any discount seats on upcoming flights. Chances are there will have been a few cancellations and you can snag some cheap tickets to somewhere. Just make sure you have a way of getting back and give yourself a while to do it. Great way of just seeing random places though.
